plain.text: The disciples asked who is the greatest in the kingdom. Jesus called a little child and said, Unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom. Whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest. Whoever welcomes a child in his name welcomes him. He warned strongly against causing little ones to stumble, and to cut off whatever causes you to sin.

Do not look down on these little ones. If a shepherd has a hundred sheep and one wanders away, he leaves the ninety-nine to look for it, and rejoices more over that one. Your Father does not want any of these little ones to be lost.

If a brother or sister sins against you, go and talk to them privately. If they won't listen, take one or two others; if they still refuse, tell the church. Jesus said that where two or three gather in his name, he is there with them.

Peter asked how many times he should forgive: up to seven times? Jesus said, not seven, but seventy-seven times. He told a story: a king forgave a servant a debt so huge he could never repay it. But that servant then seized a fellow servant who owed him a little and had him thrown into prison. The king was angry: shouldn't you have had mercy as I had mercy on you? Jesus said the Father will treat us the same way unless we forgive from the heart.

summary.bigIdea: In God's kingdom the humble are greatest, every lost one is sought, and those who have been forgiven must forgive.
points: Become humble like a little child.
The shepherd goes looking for the one lost sheep.
Forgive not seven times, but seventy-seven times.
summary.reflection: Is there someone you need to forgive, remembering how much you have been forgiven?
